note: Every number in this file is a modeling choice, even when anchored to guidance. Read rationale and source IDs before editing. No scenario probabilities or live market price are assumed.

shared.fx_rationale: Derived from management's rounded June-end net debt: INR63660m / USD672.5m. A reporting-date translation proxy, NOT a verified spot quote. USD business is valued in USD and converted once.
shared.closing_fx_rationale: Assumes the June-end translation proxy for Tega's June 1 contribution; actual transaction FX/hedge settlement remains to be reconciled.
shared.opening_bridge_rationale: June 30 legacy cash is not disclosed separately. Roll March unrestricted liquidity forward using the disclosed contribution and parent loan, Q1 Tega transaction fees, and the above cash-flow estimates. Principal repayments reduce cash and debt equally. Do not add March fundraising cash to post-acquisition equity for free.
shared.asset_rationale: Legacy March assets are rolled forward with assumed Q1 commissioning and reported Q1 D&A. Molycop annual D&A starts at June D&A x 12, split between the provisional intangible base / assumed 15-year life and a residual existing-asset charge; that residual is capitalized over 8 assumed remaining years. These are modeling asset balances, not reported PPE. No goodwill amortization or unverified acquisition tax shield.
shared.molycop_other_claims_rationale: Conservative provisional reserve based on S&P's other debt adjustments; includes unallocated lease/pension/other claims and lower-level minority/JV scope uncertainty. It is not a verified fair value or a second deduction of Apollo's ordinary interest. Sensitivity shows 0/50/100. Replace after reconciling the net-debt definition and subsidiary claims.
shared.preference_rationale: USD270m issue value is a provisional June-end fair-value proxy. Contractual return, redemption premium and exit rights are not quantified in the reviewed filings. The 12% PIK/cash schedule is an analyst stress assumption, NOT a disclosed coupon. Perpetual instrument: no invented mandatory redemption. DCF deducts today's claim once; future PIK is not subtracted again from FCFF.
shared.financing_rationale: Cash-interest and repayment schedules are estimates. USD63m interest + USD7m bank principal matches the approximate USD70m ten-month guidance, but the split is not disclosed. Lease principal is separately assumed USD3m annually, matching new lease liabilities and keeping the provisional other-claims reserve stable. Later 9% is a cash-interest/net-debt proxy, not a contractual loan rate. 70% cash retention and parent sweeps are choices, not covenants. Required new funding and contractual maturity review years are flagged.
shared.tax_rationale: Normalized marginal cash-tax assumptions; no cross-country loss sharing, acquired tax-loss benefit, or automatic deduction of PPA amortization.
shared.pending_issue_rationale: Only a separate pro-forma sensitivity adds the proposed 478435 shares and INR953.99939m cash together. Gross proceeds assumed available; issuance expenses default zero and can be edited. Main issued-share count is unchanged.

downside.rationale: Weaker demand and pricing, slower cost savings, working-capital pressure, higher discount rates; no mine-restart windfall and no earnout payment. Forecast inputs are analyst stress assumptions.

base.rationale: Consumables growth starts at management's 15%; equipment recovery is modeled at 15% after the weak Q1. Molycop starts near 5% volume and 4% EBITDA growth, using a uniform-month proxy for the undisclosed comparable ten months. USD20m cost savings phase in, with no quantified cross-selling or asset sales. First-year EBITDA already includes first-year savings: no double count. The USD20m synergy guidance is interpreted as an annual EBITDA run-rate saving once achieved; the transcript does not supply a detailed annual savings bridge. This interpretation is tested separately.

upside.rationale: Faster demand and mine recovery, modest incremental cross-selling, full USD20m savings sooner, better cash conversion and lower discount rates. Pays the full earnout. Incremental sales and timings are analyst assumptions, not management promises.
